London for Men by Burberry is a Oriental Spicy fragrance for men. London for Men was launched in 2006. The nose behind this fragrance is Antoine Maisondieu. Top notes are Cinnamon, Lavender and Bergamot; middle notes are Leather and Mimosa; base notes are Tobacco Leaf, Guaiac Wood, Opoponax and Oakmoss.

cinesia 08/03/26 09:30

I have been wearing this fragrance since 2008, so for me this review covers 18 years of experience with this scent.

It is surprisingly mild and unassuming, making it something I can wear without worrying. This makes it a keeper, something to go back to time and time again.

The main notes i've always gotten from this fragrance after 30+ minutes of applying it:
black pepper, leather, cinnamon and dry tobacco leaves.

On my skin, it is not sweet at all. It is mostly a dry black pepper aroma and an oldstyle leather aura around me. It is incredibly warm and welcoming.

At no point it is overpowering or causing headaches. The notes are very natural.

It is definitely best as a winter fragrance. It is compatible with cold weather, even snowy or almost arctic environments.

Positives: contrary to popular opinion, this is actually quite long-lived on the skin. It leaves a subtle earthy tone for the whole day. But if you are a perfume afficionado, you might disappoint that the base notes are not strong enough. After a couple of hours, it creates a noticeable aura, but it doesn't smell like you are wearing a fragrance.

Downsides: it appears to perform in a different way on different skins or different times. Some days the cinnamon is more noticeable, and the aroma resembles a sweet cinnamon roll. On other days, the black pepper is dominant.

How to wear it: on clothes and wrists. This fragrance will stay for several days on clothes.

PrayNSpray 05/14/26 15:21

Burberry London smell like Christmas. It's that simple. Does it smell exactly like a Christmas church service? No. A photorealistic tree? No. Christmas cookies? No. Burberry London smells how Christmas feels and smells, warm, cozy, safe, slightly sweet, very lightly spicy, and woody.
I bought a new bottle with the chrome cap and clear bottle. I unfortunately must report that there has certainly been a reformulation. The scent DNA is nearly identical in air, on paper and on skin so that is a huge positive. Although what used to a great performing fragrance is now simply average, in my opinion. I disagree with the reviews that say the new formulation is weak but I will agree that performance has decreased. I believe this is due to recent regulations regarding the use and dosage of oakmoss in fragrances.
New bottle designs and reformulations are often a sign of bad things but I believe London will continue serving it's purpose exactly as it should for me. I can confidently say this because I wear and love London for about 25 days out of a 365 day year. I start wearing London on December 1 and wear it right up until Christmas morning after that London goes back on the shelf. Could I wear London in fall and right through winter until spring? Absolutely! I don't scoff at anyone who decides that Burberry London is their cold weather scent. It's great. But I tend to believe that ritual is a good thing and Burberry London being my "Christmas fragrance" is something I quite enjoy.

- Overall: 8/10
- December 1 - December 25, Day or Night
- Situation/Location - December 25, 745 AM, Toronto, Canada... You wake up and smell coffee in the air and hear the familiar voices of your family. Before you go down stairs and the kids start opening presents you decide to give yourself a quick spray of London...
- Song: It's Beginning To Look Like Christmas - Bing Crosby

col0gnemeister 04/12/26 11:28

For those who are wondering whether or not the weak longevity claims are true: they are. For those who are wondering if the cologne is still worthwhile: it's not that simple. Allow me get more in depth.

In spite of the weak longevity of this cologne, I personally agree with many others that the scent is overwhelmingly pleasant. It reeks, in a great, charming way of tobacco, leather, and a bit of spice. This combination allows the cologne to thrive during the daytime and night time, but severely restricts its usage to solely fall and winter.

The moodier scent is heavy on the nose, and instantly that factor drew me in like a freshly baked hot pie sitting in a breezy windowsill. Though it is modern, it smells like what you'd imagine swinging London felt like in 1966.

Unfortunately, the classiness of this fragrance does not save it from its greatest fault: its weak projection. It sits on your skin just like body wash does after a decent shower, and this alone makes you feel that the cologne itself is only decent, and only half of what it could be.

This is the type of cologne that cannot be definitively viewed as one thing or another, because this cologne is a gem: it's left up to preference. If you enjoy the smell of this cologne, and if you're lucky, have the right skin for it to project, this fragrance may stick with you forever.

If not, it's still only up to you to decide.

I adore this scent and I went on a quest to find a vintage formula bottle to compare to the modern one as it’s one of my favourites.
To start off the modern formulas are still great and cheap. But there is a considerable difference between vintage and new for this one.
The old one is much much stronger in the tobacco and has a huge base note presence. It’s not as fresh , and the freshness picks up later in the drydown. On the new one the freshness starts up immediately and the scent has a lighter feel to it. It also does seem to last way longer as it’s much denser.
That being said if you prefer freshness a new formula might be actually better for you. But it can feel flat but only in direct comparison. To be honest I am extremely pleased with the coty formula, although mine is the black cap , I heard they changed it again. Burberry has accomplished an extraordinary feat, I must admit. They have introduced two outstanding fragrances within a single line: London for Women and London for Men. Such occurrences are exceptionally rare, and only two other duos come to mind that have achieved a similar level of success, namely Eternity/Eternity for Men and Obsession/Obsession for Men by Calvin Klein. However, let's focus on our protagonist for today, where I can confidently affirm that Antoine Maisondieu has impeccably fulfilled his assigned task. London for Men embodies both masculinity and refinement, encapsulating the essence of Britishness in a sleek bottle. Its warm and leathery-fruit heart may draw comparisons to Jo Malone's Pomegranate Noir, but the pronounced tobacco undertones swiftly establish their dominance. The undeniable innovation of this composition has sparked admiration and countless imitations. Moreover, the culinary notes present in these perfumes served as the foundation for remarkable creations, such as Tom Ford's exquisite Tobacco Vanille from the Private Blend line. It is worth noting that due to its weight, intensity, and profound aroma, London for Men thrives best during the colder months, making it an exceptional choice for winter. I wholeheartedly recommend it to all tobacco aficionados seeking olfactory delight in their fragrances.

My Rating: Highly recommended! (7/7)

M-as-Marin 11/05/25 06:03

Even after almost two decades since its launch, Burberry London continues to captivate with its unique blend of notes. This is evident in the fact that I have repurchased it three times, a testament to its lasting appeal. As many suggest, it’s one of those rare scents that actually remind fragrance enthusiasts of Christmas time.

TOP NOTES
The opening is fresh and aromatic. It took me a while to realise that this freshness is actually coming from bergamot (usually a strange note inclusion in this sort of mix), which gives a crisp edge that keeps the scent from feeling cloying, while lavender lends classic fougère freshness. Immediately beneath both, a warming thread of cinnamon and a hint of cracked pepper are present.

HEART NOTES
When the heart arrives, the perfume feels more textured. Leather shows up as a rounded, slightly sweet kind of leather — the smell of soft gloves or an old book rather than raw hide. By this stage, the cinnamon’s heat is tempered, woven into the leathery fabric, and marks a pivotal moment in the fragrance’s character: it smells like an evening where the weather is cool, the lights are warm, and every detail matters.

BASE NOTES
The dry-down shifts toward tobacco leaf, guaiac wood, opoponax — a blend of subtly smoky, resinous, woody notes.
Tobacco here is not sweet pipe tobacco; it’s drier, closer to leaf and the residual warmth of a wine-bar aromatic haze. Guaiac wood provides a creamy, woody backbone that prevents the scent from becoming overly resinous or flat.

OVERALL
A considerable amount of time has passed since 2006, and trends have changed. For me, this fragrance has stood the test of time, and nothing really captures its magic that still makes people smile when they wear it. One of the best releases from the early days of the new millennium, back in the time when fragrance houses took significant risks to give us something new and interesting.

Epic Journey Into the Bottled Yonder, 228
-------------------------------------------------------
Purchased May 2025
This week I noticed this has the same dry down, the far - hours later - dry down, as Bogart Pour Homme. There's many down thumbs to this above and that's simply wrong. The truth shall come into the light, as they say.

FatLipWill below on 09/19/2023 said so, which confirms my finding that Burberry stole the BPH dry down not to mention this came two years after BPH. Deal with it. Have to say "yours truly loves BPH more than this one", it's more brash and manly but aren't all scents situational?

Having said I love both, London can barely be oversprayed for me. It's maximum three sprays per location otherwise there's a cloying that lingers quite a while and I cannot stand cloying in anything.
Freshies are the worst at this. See, for ME the entire scent has to be genius, from the top to the bottom and everybody nowadays focusses on the top and moves on.
You guys are being fooled into the best tops with castrated bottoms. I've tested all your trendy and favourite stuff and it's become simply pedestrian. Do read on.

The more I write my reviews, the more a certain inevitable truth regarding this entire industry and community reveals itself to me - and always by happen stance. It's the strangest thing, and to be Frank (where has he gone??) my reviews suffer for it. They've become ramblings innay.

This wasn't going to be a full fledged review, but since I cannot get more out of Burberry London, since it's so basic, the review has written itself.

It's a very nice and warm, wholesome scent. But as you probably have read, it's not what I'm particularly after. In fact I don't know what I'm after in scents. I'm constantly exploring, I'm looking for something and I don't know what it is. Though I long to seek something deep and rich like the old days. But I don't want a long lingering dry down of oakmoss that easily cloys like the old days. I sense my tastes changing.

OK let's not be hard on ourselves, just the wallet ((WILL YOU PULL OUT THAT BLOODY VIOLIN) calm down John Cleese, you've never said that though a viola would suffice).

They've destroyed all our old favourites to function/perform like anything new. Reformulations are done for a reason, they're not just to cut costs but to obviously keep up with the changing landscape of this unbelievably expensive enthusiast's hobby. They make them more user friendly and welcoming to the latest generation whose balls will never descend, whose chest hair will never see the light of day.

The people who do not understand that society used to be amazing, brilliant and polite - much like Burberry. Now it's if you're rich you must be an arsehole and let it be known you're rich, ergo an arsehole. Seriously could use a violin now.

But mates, I wish somebody had informed I needed this years ago - 8 or 9 years ago in particular.
A man simply does not brag about Burberry London, though it's another tool in his shed. You must own it and if you don't know why you're missing something from your set of tools, it's the Burb. Ramble on.
8/10

P.S.:
My bottle is the clear glass with the chromed cap, juice functioning as it should. I do not suffer performance issues as many say but I do believe it could be better for the money I paid for it. Shortly after, the same chain of chemists dropped the price by $30 only to recently raise the price back to what I paid for it... I've since destroyed my violin, how about a harp?

I am extremely happy with this! Blind bought it on clearance for a great price at a local shop before a night out, only having read some reviews online and seen the notes. It smells phenomenal... IF this sort of pallate is what you're seeking.

It has this very deep, masculine scent, filled with tobacco and darkness. Not overly smoky, not super spicy and peppery either. A very smooth and elegant trench of darkness coating your presence. As for performance, it opens with what felt to me like a strong sillage (3 sprays neck, 1 chest, 1 each wrist.) However after 30-60 minutes it died down to a more intimate projection, which I think is more suitable for this scent anyways. It's strong, it's potent, and I could totally see it getting too strong if overdone, so I like the smaller sillage honestly. The longevity is slightly above average for an EDT. I'm still catching base notes about 4 hours later, which is nice for a night out. Not crazy, but certainly not bad.

Overall, great purchase. Especially if found on sale. If you want a very dark scent, well suited to nighttime and colder seasons, this is an excellent grab for budget buyers such as myself.

Navy Cut Symphony

Burberry London unfolds like a seafarer's story: a bold opening of tobacco leaves steeped in rum and molasses, cut with black pepper and cinnamon. The scent evokes the intimacy of a well-aged navy cut tobacco, dry yet intoxicating, drawing you into its spicy warmth and port wine undertones.

Then, like waves calming after a storm, it transitions—soft mimosa glows beneath supple leather, reminiscent of old taverns and worn jackets. Resinous opoponax and guaiac wood add depth, mellowing the spice into whispers. Finally, it lingers with an ambered glow, not shouting but quietly enveloping, like fading sunlight over the ocean.

Elegantly composed yet accessibly priced, this fragrance offers a timeless dance of sweetness, spice, and nostalgia—a modern ode to age-old adventures.

9/10

This is a true gentleman's fragrance a timeless classic that exudes elegance and warmth. From the moment I first sprayed it, I felt transported to a cozy evening in the heart of London.

The opening is a burst of spicy cinnamon, perfectly balanced by fresh bergamot and calming lavender. As it settles, the heart notes reveal a delightful blend of leather, rich mimosa, and hints of port wine, which feels both sophisticated and comforting. The dry-down wraps me in a warm embrace of tobacco leaf guaiac wood, and a touch of sweet opoponax a balance that’s both masculine and soft.

The design of the bottle deserves its own praise. The iconic Burberry check wrapping gives it a stylish, British flair, and it looks fantastic on any dresser.

What I love most about this fragrance is how versatile it is. Whether I’m dressing up for a formal dinner or enjoying a quiet evening at home, it feels like the perfect companion. Its longevity is impressive, lasting several hours while leaving a subtle trail that invites compliments.

For me, London for Men is more than just a scent, it's an experience. It captures the essence of sophistication and coziness that feels like a warm scarf on a crisp autumn day. Highly recommended for those who love rich, warm, and slightly sweet fragrances!

Seanhh1986 12/27/24 14:57

I cant deny it, i looooove this stuff. Im pretty much a vintage snob, and when people talk about "modernizing" old school fragrances, this is THE apex in my opinion. I dont typically like sweetness, but this is perfectly sweet and it works amazing with the tobacco and cinnamon.
This is very masculine, but not macho. Think of literally sitting in front of a fireplace with a girl on a winter night. shes snuggling up against you and youre both falling asleep with a smile on your faces. Thats the exact picture i get from this. There could certainly be a Christmas tree in the corner of the scene as well, and indeed even with all the fancy or rare stuff i own...i still wear London on christmas.
So weve all heard the main drawback...performance sucks. Its not a lie, although i get better performance than alot of people are claiming, and thats with the newer formula too. But...for those who are saying "when this came out it was much stronger and long lasting"...you arent imagining things. In fact, even though this came out in 2006, for a couple of years there was REAL oakmoss in this. Not an oakmoss accord or a bunch of synthetic evernyl, but actual oakmoss extract. If you find boxes with evernia prunastri actually listed, then you have a bottle from the first few years and it will perform alot better. Even those arent "beastmode" but it projects better and longer than the new formulas, youll get a day out of it.
In conclusion, this is one of my favorite fragrances on earth. Antoine Maisondeau created a masterpiece of modern perfumery in my opinion, and the fact that this is ~$30 is incredible to me.

Mazov 11/01/24 11:46

This is my cheaper winter fragrance this year (more expensive one being Tom Ford Eau d'Ombre Leather) and I'm really satisfied with it.

Opening is heavy of lavender and begamot, then the cinnamon joins in, this is where I think people get a 'shaving cream' type vibe, it's kind of similar to Quorum Silver, although Quorum is heavier on the woods and is a bit more versatile. But then, the leather, woods, and moss develop - it's very smooth, warm, attractive, and inviting. I get that it smells a bit too 'clean' for some people cause of that opening, but to me it just gives it a more mature feeling. It's not too overpowering or heavy- those notes lighten it a bit, and keeps it from becoming something like Spicebomb Extreme.

Like, you don't smell like a Christmas candle, but you do smell clean and put together, but with that undercurrent of the spices from the cinnamon and tobacco to warm you up. This would go great with your classic twee-jacket professor outfit (presumably from burberry lol)

That being said, 100% a cold weather scent, but suitable for basically any occasion within that. Silage is relatively strong, and it lasts for quite some time. IMO a safe blind-buy if you want something relatively cheap for cold-weather, It's a staple of any guy's winter collection.

8.6/10

Back in 2008 I was struggling a bit. My engagement had just ended, I had to move and my industry was laying people off. I didn’t have much but that Christmas I found a little bottle (maybe 50ml?) of London on sale for cheap and decided to treat myself. When I tell you I savored ever spray, saving it for weekends and special occasions.

14 years later and life is entirely different. Now I get to repurchase this bottle strictly for the sake of nostalgia and oh boy, it doesn’t disappoint one bit. This scent will always have a special place in my heart.

Fragrance has the power to make us feel a little better. To make the world look kinder and more inviting. London is like an old friend, inviting me out for a drink or two. I can’t recommend it enough. 5 billion out of ten.
Apmahg 01/28/18 13:00

Something really bugs me every time I see reviews of Burberry London. It's repeated so many times it almost feels like common wisdom. They might outnumber me, but please, if you're thinking of buying this, especially BLIND buying this, listen to me and not to them:

BURBERRY LONDON SMELLS ABSOLUTELY NOTHING LIKE A CHRISTMAS TREE!!!

I don't know exactly where this comes from. I guess the bit of lavender in the top might be convincing people they smell something piney for a minute, but it's gone in minutes after spraying. Likewise, I can imagine a thought process that goes CINNAMON = GINGERBREAD = CHRISTMAS. But the cinnamon also only sticks around briefly at the top. Rest assured, the only people who think this smells like a Christmas tree are people who grew up with plastic ones.

What Burberry London is, is a very good, if far from transcendant tobacco-leather that's available at an even better price point. For me, if it evokes anything, it's the dimly lit study of a distinguished gentleman in his smoking jacket. If that's something you're looking to add to your collection, this is a very safe buy. If you're unsatisfied, you haven't wasted much money. And most people will be be quite satisfied.

But to everyone who thinks this can only be worn for four weeks around the holidays....keep right on doing it. Let Burberry London be inescapable for four weeks of the year. It'll be great evening wear for me the rest of the year.
edge42 10/04/14 19:14

Yes! Already so many great reviews for this fragrance that are right on the money...

Burberry London is Burberry's best, no doubt. The quality is so convincing, it smells niche quality - especially that gorgeous tobacco-cherry note.

This doesn't just smell manly, this smells gentlemanly. It smells like trust, responsibility, promises kept and dreams fulfilled. Like a man that isn't on his way, he has already arrived.

London doesn't scream, "come get me!", it speaks in a stern voice "I am here". A scent that doesn't aggressively reach for attention, instead this one swoons.

Like the inside of an upper crust gentleman's club on a cool fall or winter evening - Italian brown leather couches, fine cigars, imported wood furniture, single malt scotch and success. That is what Burberry London smells like... a scent that seems to take the wearer places. It evokes thoughts and memories and awakens passions inside you more than almost any other fragrance I've ever smelled.

In a nutshell, another reviewer, ecerusen, put it best when she said:

Burberry London smells like it is a gift for being a man!
